label: Jonathan Schaffer, Monism §1.4, p.44, final…: Schaffer distinguishes pluralism from the stronger…
locator: §1.4, p.44, second clarification: priority among derivative entities
interpretation: Source reading recorded in prose only. The second clarification on p.44 says the definitions leave relative priority among derivative entities open. For monism it explicitly permits whole-to-part priority through the hierarchy, all parts equally secondary, and ultimate parts second with explanation running upward thereafter. These are allowed alternatives subject to the framework, not simultaneous requirements or a selected actual ordering. In particular the basic-cosmos dependence clause does not require every intermediate whole-to-proper-part dependence edge, and the equal-secondary option does not make an exact star mandatory. The separate p.44 exhaustiveness sentence reverses Bu labels; this reading follows the explicit definitions on pp.42–43 rather than that apparent typographical reversal. The later DS-2 compatibility comparison is analyst reasoning in docs/notes/priority-monism-framework.md, not attributed to Schaffer.
attribution: The passage states that atomism is a specific form of pluralism and that neither monism nor pluralism as defined fixes priority among derivative entities, which is the premise.
